_status: DRAFT — CLINICALLY UNVERIFIED. Every entry requires sign-off by a licensed clinician before use in a shipped app. Do not treat any value here as final.

drugs.frequency_en: twice daily (0h and 8h on day 1, then morning/evening days 2-3)
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Severe malaria (altered consciousness, severe anemia, jaundice, respiratory distress): refer for IV artesunate.
drugs.source_name: WHO Malaria Treatment Guidelines / Ethiopia National Malaria Guideline
drugs.source_detail: Standard 6-dose regimen over 3 days. Adult weight bands same as pediatric for this drug.

drugs.notes:
IV artesunate for severe malaria. Give IV (preferred) or IM. Always follow with full 3-day oral ACT once patient can tolerate oral.

Weight-based dosing:
• <20kg: 3.0 mg/kg per dose
• ≥20kg: 2.4 mg/kg per dose

Vials needed per dose:
• ≤25kg: 1 vial
• 26-50kg: 2 vials
• 51-75kg: 3 vials
• 76-100kg: 4 vials
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Below 5kg: refer immediately for specialist care.
drugs.iv_info:
[conc:20]Reconstitute:
1. Add 3ml of provided arginine/NaHCO₃ solvent to 60mg artesunate vial
2. Shake gently until clear (~1 min)
3. Final concentration = 20mg/ml → draw [ml]ml

Give slow IV over 1-2 min (do NOT further dilute for IV push).
Use within 1 hour of reconstitution.

Always follow with full 3-day oral ACT once patient can swallow.
Monitor Hb weekly for 4 weeks for post-artesunate delayed hemolysis (PADH).
drugs.safety_warning: Monitor for post-artesunate delayed hemolysis (PADH) — check Hb weekly for 4 weeks after treatment.
drugs.source_detail: ≥20kg: 2.4mg/kg at 0, 12, 24h. Reconstitute with 3ml solvent = 20mg/ml.

drugs.notes: Used for P. vivax malaria (with Primaquine). Adult dose capped at 600mg base total.
drugs.source_detail: 25mg base/kg total over 3 days (10/10/5mg/kg). Adult max 600mg base per dose on days 1-2.

drugs.safety_warning: Primaquine can cause dangerous hemolysis in patients with G6PD deficiency. VERIFY current Ethiopian protocol on G6PD testing requirement before dosing at this facility level.
drugs.source_name: Ethiopia national low-dose radical cure protocol (rolled out nationally 2018)
drugs.source_detail: 0.25mg/kg/day for 14 days. Adult dosing same as pediatric.

drugs.source_name: WHO pneumonia treatment guideline / Ethiopia STG
drugs.source_detail: 40mg/kg/dose BID for adults. Max 3g/day. Capsule formulations available for adult patients.

drugs.notes: For severe pneumonia not responding to oral antibiotics or unable to take oral. Administer IV over 30 minutes.
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Signs of severe respiratory distress: refer for higher-level care.
drugs.iv_info:
Reconstitute:
• 1g vial + 9.6ml sterile water = 100mg/ml → draw [ml]ml

Infuse over 30 min.
Do NOT use calcium-containing fluids (Ringer's, Hartmann's).
drugs.source_detail: 50-100mg/kg/day divided q12h. Max 4g/day.
500mg day 1, 250mg days 2-5. Tablet formulation for adults.

drugs.notes: Standard adult dose: 625mg (500mg/125mg) PO BID or 1g (875mg/125mg) PO BID for severe infections.
drugs.source_detail: 625mg PO BID for moderate, 1g PO BID for severe infections.

drugs.dose_display_en:
WHO PLAN A — Some Dehydration:
Give ORS based on dehydration status (not weight alone)

Mild dehydration: 50ml/kg over 4 hours
Moderate dehydration: 75-100ml/kg over 4 hours

Severe dehydration → IV therapy (PLAN C)

Encourage additional ORS as patient desires.
Continue breastfeeding/feeding.
Reassess after 4 hours.

If no signs of dehydration: give ORS to replace ongoing losses (10ml/kg per loose stool).
drugs.notes: ORS volume depends on dehydration status. For adults, encourage drinking freely — aim for 200-400ml per loose stool.
drugs.source_detail: Adult ORS: same formulation as pediatric. Volume based on dehydration assessment.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Zinc 20mg once daily for 14 days (adult dose)

Evidence suggests benefit in zinc-deficient populations.
Consider 20mg elemental zinc daily.
drugs.source_detail: Adult dose 20mg daily for 14 days. Evidence strongest in malnourished populations.

drugs.drug_name_en: Ringer's Lactate IV (Plan C — severe dehydration)
drugs.dose_display_en:
WHO PLAN C — Severe Dehydration (Adult)
Total: 100 ml/kg IV Ringer's Lactate

Step 1: 30 ml/kg IV over 30 minutes
Step 2: 70 ml/kg IV over 2.5 hours

Reassess every 15-30 minutes.
Give ORS 5ml/kg/hour once patient can drink.
OR: 1-2L NS/RL rapid IV then 200ml/hr until rehydrated.
drugs.notes: WHO Plan C for severe dehydration with diarrhea. Use Ringer's Lactate first line. Normal Saline if RL unavailable.
drugs.safety_warning: Reassess every 15-30 minutes during IV therapy. Monitor for signs of fluid overload (crackles, raised JVP).
drugs.source_detail: 100ml/kg total. Adult: 30ml/kg over 30min + 70ml/kg over 2.5hrs.

drugs.notes: For severe bacterial gastroenteritis / dysentery (Salmonella, Shigella). 2g daily divided q12h or single daily dose.
drugs.source_detail: 1-2g IV daily for severe dysentery.

drugs.notes: Adult max 1g per dose. Max 4g per day. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
drugs.safety_warning: Do not exceed 4g per 24 hours. Risk of hepatotoxicity at higher doses. Avoid in severe liver disease.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg-1g PO q4-6h PRN. Max 4g/day.

drugs.notes: Standard adult dose: 400mg PO every 6-8 hours. Range 200-800mg/dose. Max 2.4g/day.
drugs.safety_warning: Avoid in dehydration, active peptic ulcer, renal impairment, or aspirin allergy. Caution in elderly.
drugs.source_detail: 400mg PO q6-8h PRN. Max 2.4g/day.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Cotrimoxazole 960mg (800mg/160mg) PO twice daily for 3-5 days

Or 2 tablets of 400mg/80mg strength twice daily

Duration: 3 days for uncomplicated, 5-7 days for complicated UTI.
drugs.notes: Check local resistance patterns. Cotrimoxazole resistance is rising — consider alternatives if no improvement in 48 hours.
drugs.safety_warning: Caution in G6PD deficiency, renal impairment, elderly, and sulfonamide allergy.
drugs.source_detail: 960mg (DS) PO BID. Duration 3-7 days per local guidelines.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Amoxicillin 500mg PO three times daily for 5-7 days

Or 1g PO twice daily.
drugs.notes: Increasing resistance in E. coli. Use only if local susceptibility confirmed or as second-line.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO TID or 1g PO BID for 5-7 days.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Ceftriaxone 1g IV/IM once daily for 5-7 days

Or 1g IV every 12 hours for severe/complicated UTI.

For uncomplicated: 1g single dose IM or IV may be sufficient per some guidelines.
drugs.iv_info:
Reconstitute:
• 1g vial + 3.6ml sterile water for IM = 250mg/ml
• 1g vial + 9.6ml sterile water for IV = 100mg/ml

Inject IM deep in gluteal muscle.
Infuse IV over 2-4 minutes or 30 min infusion.
drugs.source_detail: 1g IV/IM daily. 1-2g daily for severe infections.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Amoxicillin 500mg PO three times daily for 7-10 days

Or 1g PO twice daily.

Important: 10-day course for confirmed Group A Strep to prevent rheumatic fever.
drugs.duration_warning: IMPORTANT: 10-day duration for strep eradication — do NOT default to 5 days.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO TID × 10 days for strep pharyngitis. 10 days critical for rheumatic fever prevention.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Azithromycin 500mg PO once daily for 3-5 days

Or 500mg on day 1, then 250mg days 2-5.

Penicillin-allergy alternative.
drugs.notes: Penicillin-allergy alternative
drugs.source_detail: 500mg day 1, 250mg days 2-5 for tonsillopharyngitis.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Acute asthma exacerbation:

Inhaler (MDI) with spacer:
  2-4 puffs (100mcg each) every 20 min for 1st hour
  Then 2-4 puffs every 3-4 hours as needed

Nebulized:
  5mg (1mL of 0.5% solution) in 3mL NS every 20 min × 3 doses
  Then 5mg every 4-6 hours as needed

For COPD:
  Inhaler: 2 puffs (100-200mcg) q4-6h PRN
drugs.notes: First-line rescue bronchodilator for acute asthma and COPD exacerbations.
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Acute severe asthma: unable to speak in sentences, RR >30, SpO2 <90%, use of accessory muscles — refer urgently.
drugs.safety_warning: Tremor, tachycardia, and palpitations are common side effects. Use with caution in ischemic heart disease.
drugs.source_name: GINA Guidelines / Ethiopia STG for Asthma
drugs.source_detail: Adult: 2-4 puffs MDI via spacer PRN. Nebulized 5mg per dose for acute exacerbations.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Prednisolone 40-50mg PO once daily for 5-7 days

For acute exacerbation not responding to bronchodilators.
No taper needed for courses <7 days.
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Life-threatening asthma: silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, altered consciousness — refer immediately.
drugs.safety_warning: Short-term use generally safe. Monitor for hyperglycemia, especially in diabetic patients.
drugs.source_detail: 40-50mg PO daily × 5-7 days for acute exacerbations. 1mg/kg/day commonly used.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Aminophylline IV (second-line — only if inadequate response to salbutamol + steroids):

Loading dose: 5mg/kg IV over 30 min (if not on oral theophylline)
Maintenance: 0.5-0.7 mg/kg/hour IV infusion

Monitoring required: Check pulse, BP, and signs of toxicity.

Therapeutic range: 10-20 mcg/mL (theophylline level).
drugs.notes: Second-line for severe refractory asthma. Narrow therapeutic window — toxicity risk is significant. Only use if salbutamol + prednisolone inadequate and referral not possible.
drugs.safety_warning: Narrow therapeutic window. Toxicity: tachyarrhythmias, seizures, vomiting. Reduce dose in heart failure, liver disease, and elderly. Monitor theophylline levels if available. Avoid with ciprofloxacin, cimetidine, and macrolides (increase levels).
drugs.source_name: GINA / BTS Guidelines — second-line acute asthma
drugs.source_detail: 5mg/kg loading (if no recent theophylline), then 0.5-0.7mg/kg/hr. Use only in severe refractory cases.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5-25mg PO once daily

Start: 12.5mg daily
Titrate: 25mg daily if needed

Max: 50mg daily (higher doses offer little extra benefit with more side effects).

Take in the morning (morning diuresis).

Often combined with other agents (ACEi, ARB, CCB) as combination therapy.
drugs.notes: First-line thiazide diuretic for hypertension. Start low, go slow. Monitor electrolytes (K+, Na+).
drugs.safety_warning: Monitor K+ and Na+ levels (risk of hypokalemia, hyponatremia). Caution in gout (raises uric acid), diabetes (may raise glucose), and renal impairment.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian HTN guideline / JNC 8
drugs.source_detail: First-line: 12.5-25mg daily. Max 50mg/day. Check electrolytes at follow-up.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Amlodipine 5mg PO once daily

Start: 5mg daily
Titrate: 10mg daily if needed after 2-4 weeks

Max: 10mg daily
drugs.notes: Calcium channel blocker. Well tolerated. No lab monitoring needed. Effective in African patients.
drugs.safety_warning: Common: ankle edema, headache, flushing. Caution in heart failure with reduced EF. Avoid grapefruit juice.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian HTN guideline / JNC 8
drugs.source_detail: 5-10mg daily. First-line for African patients per ALLHAT trial evidence.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Enalapril 5-10mg PO once daily

Start: 5mg daily
Titrate: 10-20mg daily if needed

Max: 40mg daily (usually divided BID at higher doses)
drugs.notes: ACE inhibitor. Particularly beneficial in diabetes, heart failure, and CKD with proteinuria.
drugs.safety_warning: Check K+ and creatinine before starting and after 1-2 weeks. Contraindicated in pregnancy (do not use if pregnancy possible). Common: dry cough, angioedema (rare but serious). Avoid or reduce dose in renal impairment.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian HTN guideline / JNC 8
drugs.source_detail: 5-20mg daily. First-line in diabetic patients. Check renal function before start and 1-2 weeks after.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Methyldopa 250mg PO twice daily (for hypertensive urgency / second-line)

Start: 250mg BID
Titrate: 500mg BID if needed (max 2g/day)

Note: Preferred use in pregnancy (safest antihypertensive in pregnancy).

Not first-line for routine HTN due to side effect profile.
drugs.notes: Centrally acting agent. Not first-line for routine HTN. Used in pregnancy or when other agents contraindicated.
drugs.safety_warning: Sedation, dizziness, dry mouth, depression, orthostatic hypotension. May cause hemolytic anemia (rare). Monitor LFTs.
drugs.source_detail: 250-500mg PO BID. Preferred agent in pregnancy. Max 2g/day.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Metformin 500mg PO twice daily (with meals)

Start: 500mg once daily for 1 week (reduce GI side effects)
Titrate: increase by 500mg weekly to target 1g BID

Standard maintenance: 500mg BID or 1g BID

Max: 2.55g (3 tablets of 850mg) per day

Extended-release available: 500mg-2g once daily.
drugs.notes: First-line oral hypoglycemic for Type 2 Diabetes. Biguanide class. Does NOT cause hypoglycemia as monotherapy.
drugs.safety_warning: Contraindicated in eGFR <30 (risk of lactic acidosis). Stop if: severe infection, dehydration, surgery, contrast dye (hold 48h post). GI side effects (diarrhea, nausea) common — start low, go slow. Monitor B12 with long-term use.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian DM guideline / ADA 2025
drugs.source_detail: First-line for T2DM. 500mg BID, titrate to 1g BID. Max 2.55g/day.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Gliclazide 80mg PO twice daily

Or Gliclazide MR 30mg once daily (modified release)

Start: 40-80mg daily
Titrate: up to 160mg BID (standard) or 120mg once daily (MR)

Max: 320mg/day (standard immediate release)
drugs.notes: Sulfonylurea. Second-line after metformin or if metformin contraindicated. Stimulates pancreatic insulin secretion.
drugs.safety_warning: CAUTION: Can cause hypoglycemia, especially in elderly, renal impairment, or missed meals. Educate patient on hypoglycemia symptoms. Weight gain possible.
drugs.source_detail: 80-320mg daily IR or 30-120mg MR daily. Second-line after metformin.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Insulin NPH — Starting regimen:

Total daily dose: 0.2-0.3 units/kg/day (T2DM)

Once-daily regimen:
  NPH 10 units SC at bedtime (or morning)
  Increase by 2 units every 3 days until fasting glucose <130mg/dL

Twice-daily regimen:
  2/3 dose AM, 1/3 dose PM

Assess: Fasting glucose to titrate. Check for hypoglycemia.
drugs.notes: Insulin for T2DM: when oral agents fail (HbA1c >9% or symptomatic hyperglycemia). NPH insulin is the most available in Ethiopian public sector.
drugs.safety_warning: HIGH-ALERT MEDICATION. Hypoglycemia risk. Patient must have glucometer and hypoglycemia education. Store in refrigerator (2-8°C). Do NOT freeze. Reduce dose in renal impairment.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian DM guideline / ADA 2025
drugs.source_detail: Start with 0.2-0.3 IU/kg/day NPH. Tirate to fasting glucose target. NPH most available in Ethiopia.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Omeprazole 20mg PO once daily

For dyspepsia/GERD:
  20mg once daily before breakfast × 4-8 weeks

For H. pylori eradication (triple therapy):
  20mg BID + amoxicillin 1g BID + clarithromycin 500mg BID × 14 days

For gastric ulcer:
  20-40mg once daily × 4-8 weeks
drugs.notes: Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI). First-line for dyspepsia, GERD, and peptic ulcer disease.
drugs.safety_warning: Long-term use (>1 year) associated with B12 deficiency, osteoporosis risk, GI infections (C. diff), hypomagnesemia. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
drugs.source_name: Ethiopia STG / WHO EML / ACG guidelines
drugs.source_detail: 20mg daily for dyspepsia. 40mg for severe esophagitis or H. pylori therapy component.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Ranitidine 150mg PO twice daily

For dyspepsia/GERD:
  150mg BID × 4-8 weeks

For maintenance:
  150mg once daily at bedtime
drugs.notes: H2 receptor antagonist. Second-line after PPIs. Now less preferred due to NDMA impurity concerns in some formulations.
drugs.safety_warning: Less effective than PPIs. May cause confusion in elderly. Check for drug interactions (warfarin, theophylline, phenytoin).
drugs.source_detail: 150mg PO BID or 300mg at bedtime.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Antacid 10-20ml PO as needed for symptom relief

Or 1-2 tablets chewed 1 hour after meals and at bedtime.

Maximum: do not exceed 8 doses per 24 hours.

For mild, intermittent dyspepsia only. Not for chronic treatment.
drugs.notes: Over-the-counter option for mild intermittent symptoms. Provides rapid but short-lived relief.
drugs.safety_warning: May interfere with absorption of other drugs (tetracyclines, iron, digoxin, thyroxine, fluoroquinolones). Take 2 hours apart from other medications. Caution in renal impairment (magnesium toxicity).
drugs.source_detail: Symptom relief only. Not for long-term management of dyspepsia or GERD.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Cloxacillin 500mg PO four times daily (6-hourly) for 5-7 days

For cellulitis: 500mg-1g PO QID × 5-7 days.

Max: 4g/day.

Take on empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals).
drugs.notes: Antistaphylococcal penicillin. First-line for skin infections (impetigo, cellulitis, abscess).
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO QID for skin/soft tissue infections. 1g PO QID for severe cellulitis.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Amoxicillin 500mg PO three times daily for 5-7 days

Less effective for Staph. Consider cloxacillin first if Staph suspected.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO TID. Second-line for skin infections.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Ceftriaxone 2g IV once daily for 7-14 days

Or 1g IV every 12 hours.

Duration:
  Uncomplicated: 7-10 days
  Severe: 10-14 days

First-line for severe typhoid or if quinolone resistance suspected.
drugs.notes: Third-generation cephalosporin. First-line for severe typhoid fever given increasing fluoroquinolone resistance. Effective against Salmonella typhi.
drugs.iv_info:
Reconstitute:
• 1g vial + 9.6ml sterile water = 100mg/ml

Infuse over 30 minutes.
For IM: 1g + 3.6ml lidocaine 1% or sterile water.
drugs.source_name: WHO Guidelines for Typhoid Fever / Ethiopia STG
drugs.source_detail: 2g IV daily × 7-14 days. First-line for severe typhoid due to resistance patterns.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Azithromycin 500mg PO once daily for 7 days

Or 1g single dose for uncomplicated.

Effective alternative for uncomplicated typhoid.
Particularly useful when fluoroquinolone resistance suspected.

Safe in pregnancy.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO daily × 7 days for uncomplicated typhoid. Alternative if ceftriaxone not available.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO twice daily for 7-10 days

Or 400mg IV twice daily for severe cases.

Note: Increasing resistance — use only if susceptibility confirmed.

Duration: 7-10 days for uncomplicated, 10-14 days for severe.
drugs.notes: Fluoroquinolone. Once first-line for typhoid but now limited by increasing resistance in Ethiopia and globally. Use only when susceptibility confirmed.
drugs.safety_warning: NOT first-line due to resistance. Avoid in pregnancy and children (tendon damage risk). Caution in epilepsy, elderly, and with NSAIDs (CNS side effects). May prolong QT interval.
drugs.source_name: WHO Guidelines for Typhoid Fever — resistance warning
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO BID × 7-10 days. Resistance increasing — use with caution.
